svg.title: Figure 2 — Swin-Tiny phase classifier with dihedral TTA
svg.text: Figure 2 | Stage-4 classifier: Swin-Tiny with dihedral test-time augmentation and temporal post-processing
One 256 × 256 segmented crop per frame → 8 equivalent views → Swin-Tiny → averaged posterior → median-smoothed phase timeline
patch merging halves the token grid and doubles the channel width between stages
attention runs inside 7 × 7 windows; the window grid shifts by half a
window in the next block, which is what connects them
Why a windowed transformer here: five-fold twin symmetry is a whole-particle relation,
The crystallographic phase of a particle is
invariant under rotation and reflection — a
decahedron rotated by 90° is still a decahedron.
So the 8 dihedral views are 8 genuinely
equivalent observations of the same label.
p̄(c | frame) = ⅛ Σ softmax( f( g·x ) )
g ∈ D₄, no retraining, 8× inference cost
Stack per-frame posteriors into a T × 3 array
Median-filter each class stream over 11 frames — the median kills isolated
single-frame flips but preserves a step, which is what a real phase change is
argmax → group equal-label runs → absorb runs shorter than 10 frames
Inside each Ih-family segment, query a second model trained without
Ih→Dh: p(Ih) > 0.6 ∧ p(Ih) > p(Dh)+0.2 → Ih; mirror → Dh; otherwise Ih→Dh
written as timeline.png, segments.csv (start / end / duration / label / confidence) and an overlay MP4
while the fringe evidence that separates the phases is local — a shifted-window model has both.
backbone loaded from a prior 3-class ckpt;
needed to escape the imbalance minimum
